content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani revealed on Monday what was going through his mind during the viral moment when he stood beside President Trump with a blank expression as the president launched a blistering attack on the media.

This week on his New York-taped talk show, host Jimmy Kimmel praised Mamdani's "restraint" as Trump attacked CNN, MS NOW and Politico and barred them from the White House:

"That was really impressive," Kimmel said. "When I saw that clip I thought: 'Well, this is definitely not a guy I would want to play poker with.'"

Not only did Mamdani defend the press at the joint press conference, he also personally called each of the news organizations Trump had ordered shut out.

But, as Kimmel noted, Trump appeared entirely unbothered.

"He just seems to like you, that's the thing," Kimmel said. "And I think that seems to be the only thing that matters."

So what was Mamdani actually thinking when Trump attacked the press? A kind of negotiating art, given that he is working with Trump on a major real estate project.

"The thing we've been talking about most recently is the Sunnyside Yard, this idea that has been talked about for decades about putting a platform over the freight rail yard and then building 12,000 units of housing on top of it," Mamdani said. "So at that moment, with the closeup shot, I was thinking about 12,000 units of housing, 30,000 jobs, the largest housing development since the early 1970s."

Kimmel offered Mamdani another suggestion that might help close the deal.

He quipped: "Have you considered renaming it Trumpyside Yard?"

Mamdani said: "I had not considered that."
